facts.text: The "Stammbaumtheorie" is a theory of language evolution.
The "Stammbaumtheorie" posited that languages develop from a common ancestral language through diversification.
Wilhelm Wundt wrote "Elements of Folk Psychology".
Wilhelm Wundt studied word meanings in connection with "Elements of Folk Psychology".
Leonard Bloomfield published "Introduction to the Study of Language" in 1916.
Leonard Bloomfield presented a theory of meaning based on the distribution of words in a sentence.
Leonard Bloomfield argued that the meaning of a word is determined by its syntactic relationships with other words in the sentence.
Ferdinand de Saussure published "Course in General Linguistics" in 1918.
"Course in General Linguistics" laid the foundations for structural linguistics.
Structural linguistics focused on the analysis of language structure and the relationships between words in a sentence.
